rationale: 01-qbsort is a tiny McCat benchmark dominated by sort kernels (quicksort partition loops, bubble-sort inner loops) where the workload itself is the hot path, so the table favors low-overhead passes: SUB and SPLIT get high security/diversity weights with low cost sensitivity because they are cheap, safe, and SPLIT seeds diversity for other passes; FLA is weighted highest on SecurityGain since control-flow flattening gives the strongest reverse-engineering resistance on loop- and branch-heavy sort logic, tempered by moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so it is applied selectively rather than to the hottest innermost loops; BCF is deliberately de-emphasized (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk sensitivity) because its bogus-block overhead compounds badly in tight sorting loops and bloats a very small binary; IBR and IGV sit in the middle, adding indirection-based resistance on branch- and array-access-heavy code at acceptable cost; ICALL is kept modest with elevated RuntimeCost weight because qbsort's recursion and frequent small calls make indirect-call dispatch overhead disproportionately visible. Overall the profile lacks function-level data (empty source profile), so weights are set conservatively to let feature-driven selection apply strong passes where features justify them while capping expensive or risky transformations.
